leftEvidence.title: Covenant memory frames the Exodus promise

points.label: Covenant setting
points.left: Covenant memory is explicitly connected to the unfolding Exodus rather than treated as an isolated ancestral event.
points.right: The scene places covenant response after rescue from Egypt, before the covenant words are publicly ratified.

points.label: Parties, action, or promise
points.left: Yahweh remembers · Moses · Israel · Abraham · Isaac · Jacob · Bring out · redeem · take as people · bring into land · I will be your God
points.right: Israel · Moses · Sinai · Hear voice · keep covenant · Treasured possession · kingdom of priests · holy nation

payload.posture: Exodus 6 invokes the ancestors; Exodus 19 addresses the delivered nation with conditional covenant language.
payload.tension: The two sources materially share covenant language or memory, while their parties, setting, action, or literary purpose remain distinct.
payload.title: Covenant with the ancestors / covenant at Sinai
